title: Beta2-adrenergic agonist salbutamol exhibits enantioselective disposition in skeletal muscle of lean young men following oral administration
authors: Hostrup M, Jacobson GA, Eibye K, Narkowicz CK, Nichols DS, Jessen S
population: Healthy lean men aged 19-32 years, beta2-agonist naive, one oral dose of 24 mg salbutamol with a light meal
funder: The study was supported by the Danish Ministry of Culture and Anti-Doping Danmark.
result: The pharmacological actions of salbutamol reside with the (R)-enantiomer, the (S)-enantiomer being regarded as pharmacodynamically inert. After 24 mg orally, mean arterial plasma concentrations were about 10-fold higher for (S)- than (R)-salbutamol: 33 (range 9-62) ng/ml and 49 (30-84) ng/ml for (S)-salbutamol against 4 (1-6) ng/ml and 4 (2-5) ng/ml for (R)-salbutamol at 2.5 h and 7 h. Vastus lateralis concentrations were 0.17 (0.1-0.26) against 0.04 (0.02-0.06) ng/mg dry weight at 2.5 h and 0.31 (0.21-0.46) against 0.06 (0.04-0.12) ng/mg at 7 h. The median muscle:plasma partition coefficient at 7 h was 3.69 (2.4-14.1) for (R)-salbutamol and 0.99 (0.5-3.9) for (S)-salbutamol (p = 0.003).
